issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 4.4 applies scalar Hoeffding's inequality entry-wise to the random variables $(S_\calX f)(y_{l,j})$ for an individual, fixed observable $f \in \bH$. This only proves that for each fixed $f$, the bound holds with probability at least $1 - 2d\exp(-m\veps^2 / (2\|k\|_\infty))$. The proof then incorrectly infers that on an event of that same probability, the bound holds simultaneously for all $f \in \bH$ (and Theorem 2.3 restates this as a uniform operator norm bound). Since $(S_\calX f)(y_{l,j})$ depends on $f$, the universal quantifier over $f \in \bH$ cannot be exchanged with the probability without taking a supremum over the infinite-dimensional unit ball of $\bH$ (or the $d$-dimensional subspace $V_\calX$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the scalar Hoeffding bound on $(S_\calX f)(y_{l,j})$ with a vector/Hilbert-space Hoeffding inequality applied directly to the mean-zero canonical feature vectors $\Phi_{y_{l,j}} - \bE[\Phi_Y \mid X=x_j]$ in $\bH$, which are bounded in norm by $2\|k\|_\infty^{1/2}$. Applying Cauchy-Schwarz in $\bH$ then bounds $|g_j - g_j^\mathrm{MC}| \le \|f\|_\bH \|\frac{1}{m}\sum_{l=1}^m (\Phi_{y_{l,j}} - \bE[\Phi_Y \mid X=x_j])\|_\bH$ uniformly for all $f \in \bH$ with probability at least $1 - 2d\exp(-m\veps^2 / (8\|k\|_\infty))$, restoring the uniform bounds up to the constant in the exponent.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform-over-$f$ and operator-norm $L^\infty$-error guarantees claimed in Theorems 2.3, 2.4, 4.4 and Corollaries 4.6, 4.7, C.2, C.3 do not follow from the argument as written.
issues.title: Quantifier exchange in Monte Carlo error bound across observable space
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument using Hilbert-space concentration on the RKHS feature vectors restores the advertised uniform operator error bounds without altering the overarching architecture, parameter rates, or advertised scope, changing only a numerical constant in the exponential probability tail.
